content.text:
I submitted **index 29** (Mg 0.19, Sb 0.81) as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.087%, the highest of the three samples I measured, though all three values are low.

| Index | Mg fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 29 | 0.19 | 0.0867 |
| 26 | 0.27 | 0.068 |
| 10 | 0.76 | about 0 (−0.00006) |

- **Why I measured the Sb-rich end first:** the models predicted band gaps below the 3.2 eV photon energy there (MgSb2O6 2.8 eV, MgSb4O8 2.6 eV), so those phases should absorb the light. The Mg-rich Mg4Sb2O9 is predicted at 4.2 eV and should not absorb.
- **What the measurements showed:** the Mg-rich sample gave essentially nothing, and EQE rose toward the Sb-rich end. Index 29 is the most Sb-rich composition in the library, so I couldn't test whether the trend keeps going.
- **XRD didn't identify the phase:** I used 2 of the 5 scans (indices 25 and 19). Both show the same four peaks, which fit a simple cubic lattice, but none of the known phases I compared against matched well (best similarity 0.30). The band-gap reasoning above therefore rests on the models, not on confirmed phases.

With only 3 measurements, most of the middle of the composition range (Mg 0.3 to 0.7) went unmeasured. A better composition there can't be ruled out.
